newsitem.title: USA: Colombian drug leader to be tried in United States.
newsitem.headline: Colombian drug leader to be tried in United States.

text.p: An alleged top-ranking Colombian drug cartel leader pleaded not guilty at his arraignment in federal court on Tuesday to charges he was involved in a six-year cocaine smuggling operation.
Justo Pastor Perafan, or "The Big Boss," is accused of allegedly transporting more than 30 tons of cocaine into the United States between 1988 and 1994, prosecutors said.

He was charged with eight counts of illegal activity, including conspiracy, continuing criminal enterprise and possession and distribution of a controlled substance. Perafan pleaded not guilty to all of the charges in the federal courthouse on Long Island.

He was indicted almost two years ago after federal agents allegedly found 600 pounds (272 kilograms) of cocaine hidden in the cross beams of one of his trucks in a warehouse, Drug Enforcement Administration officials said.

Perafan, who was being sought by both the United States and authorities in his native Colombia where he faces charges that he earned money illegally, was arrested in April in Venezuela, officials said. He had undergone hair transplants and possibly plastic surgery to conceal his identity, DEA investigators said.

Last Thursday the Venezuelan Supreme Court ruled Perafan should be extradited to the United States. He was flown from Caracas to the small Republic Airport in Farmingdale, N.Y., early on Saturday under tight security, officials said.
U.S. Attorney General Janet Reno "congratulated" the Venezuelan government for allowing Perafan to stand trial for "the serious crimes for which he is accused."
If convicted Perafan faces a minimum of 20 years in jail and more than $2 million in fines, U.S. District Attorney Zachary Carter said.

Perafan was "in the upper eschelons" of the notorious Cali drug cartel, according to a DEA official. He was allegedly at the helm of a massive New York-based drug distribution network dubbed "The Company," the official said.
